feedback: Iterations 0 and 1 both leave the s-bend and slalom off track at mean max_error of about 0.060 to 0.062 m, with line-loss events at 1 to 2 per run (iteration 1 table). Moving the sensors from y = 0.04 to 0.06 m and raising kp to 2.0 gave the first finishes on the oval (4 of 20) and raised s-bend progress to 0.206, so forward look-ahead is helping. Because line losses stayed low, the failure is drift on the bends, not lost sensing. Oval oscillation rose from 0.07 to 0.18 at the higher gain, so more gain alone is probably not the answer. For the next race, hold the geometry (five sensors, x = ±0.024 m, y = 0.06 m, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.8 kg). Do not change the body, since body width cannot widen the off-track limit. Keep the spread at ±0.024 m while line_loss_events stay at or below about 2 per run. If the next race shows the s-bend and slalom still hitting max_error near 0.06 m with progress below 0.25 and oscillation high, the next geometry lever is mass: try about 0.6 kg to cut yaw inertia. If line losses rise above about 2 per run on the sharpest bend, widen to x = ±0.032 m. I state no outcome for the next candidate.
